channel.title: Investment Banking Blog
channel.description: Sourced explainers, case studies, and commentary.

item.title: Lord Stanley Fink at Britannia: what a chairman appointment changes
item.description: Corporate-governance analysis. The company announcement and August 2026 director filing provide a starting point for assessing board oversight and responsibilities.

item.title: The August 2026 anti-weaponization fund rescission: reading the order
item.description: Public-records analysis. The Justice Department revoked the order establishing the fund. Separate records are needed to assess payments, settlements, or future proposals.

item.title: Banco Caracas and Santander: reading the 2000 acquisition record
item.description: Historical analysis. Santander’s acquisition announcement explains the proposed ownership change and scale of the combined banks. Here is how to read that record.

item.title: Seattle’s July 2026 police-chief transition: questions for accountability
item.description: Case study. The mayor accepted Shon Barnes’s resignation and named an interim chief. Reviewing the incident response requires a separate timeline.

item.title: Pentagon casualty categories: why consistent definitions matter
item.description: Public-records analysis. A change in reporting categories can alter a subtotal without changing the overall toll. Comparable definitions make scrutiny possible.

item.title: USTR’s July 2026 tariff action: interpreting rates and exemptions
item.description: Trade-policy analysis. The action specified rates of 10% or 12.5% for 60 trading partners. Product coverage and entry rules determine the effect on an import.

item.title: H.R. 9770: what the House’s July 2026 funding vote established
item.description: Policy analysis. The House passed the stopgap measure 220–205. The vote illustrates the difference between one chamber’s approval and enacted funding.

item.title: Hill Country flood safety: how to use warnings and river information
item.description: Preparedness guide. Use current local warnings, respect road closures, and plan routes that avoid low crossings. This is a preparedness guide, not a live alert.

item.title: Inside the Supreme Court’s budget
item.description: Policy analysis. The July 2026 hearing discussed security and operations. Recurring costs, one-time investments, and enacted amounts are different measures.

item.title: When the S&P 500 rises but most stocks fall: the July 6 example
item.description: Case study. The July 2026 session illustrates the difference between an index’s return and the number of companies participating in its gains.

item.title: Kiros’s Colorado primary victory: what one contest can tell us
item.description: Election analysis. The 2026 result changed the Democratic nominee in Colorado’s 1st District. Local evidence is needed to explain why voters chose the challenger.

item.title: SpaceX’s IPO: distinguish offer proceeds from company value
item.description: Offering analysis. SpaceX’s June 2026 filing shows why the offer price, gross proceeds, net proceeds, and company valuation are different figures.

item.title: Futures, opening prices, and the close: lessons from June 9, 2026
item.description: Case study. The chip-led rebound illustrates why the time of a quote matters when interpreting a market report.

item.title: The CFTC’s Santos order: integrity questions for event contracts
item.description: Regulatory analysis. The July 2026 order imposed a $35,000 penalty. The case raises questions about traders who can influence an underlying event.

item.title: The SEC’s May 2026 climate-disclosure proposal: how to read its scope
item.description: Regulatory analysis. The proposal concerned the 2024 disclosure framework. Investors still need to assess material business risks and other reporting obligations.

item.title: O’Hara’s Minneapolis resignation: allegations, findings, and oversight
item.description: Legal case study. The May 2026 departure shows why findings about interference must be separated from the underlying relationship allegations.

item.title: Why diplomatic headlines moved stocks and oil in May 2026
item.description: Case study. Two trading sessions show how changing expectations about shipping and energy supplies can move different markets.

item.title: The 2026 Raúl Castro indictment: separating the event from the prosecution
item.description: Legal case study. The case concerns the 1996 aircraft shootdown. The later charging action raises separate questions about allegations, procedure, and custody.

item.title: Reading the FBI’s May 2026 San Diego mosque-attack updates
item.description: Public-safety case study. The agency’s statements provide a dated record of the response. They also show why early investigative and casualty information needs attribution.

item.title: Kevin Warsh’s Fed appointment: the timeline and the chair’s role
item.description: Case study. Warsh took office on May 22, 2026. The transition explains how confirmation, Board membership, and FOMC leadership fit together.

item.title: JPMorgan’s 2026 leadership reshuffle: what it means for investment banking
item.description: Case study. Three co-heads share global investment banking leadership. The practical questions concern client coordination, responsibility, and execution.

item.title: Goldman’s May 2026 rate-cut forecast: why the date mattered
item.description: Forecast analysis. Goldman’s May forecast illustrates how an energy shock can shift the expected path of interest rates.

item.title: The LAUSD Title IX inquiry: what an investigation can establish
item.description: Legal case study. The Education Department’s May 2026 announcement raised questions about complaint handling. The inquiry itself did not establish a violation.

item.title: Elon Musk’s five-step process: a practical reading
item.description: Management explainer. A practical way to apply the five steps: challenge requirements, remove duplication, simplify, speed up, and automate.

item.title: Fed chair, governor, and FOMC chair: three roles in one transition
item.description: Institutional explainer. The May 2026 leadership transition shows why the Fed’s offices, appointment dates, and policy votes need to be understood separately.

item.title: Alaska’s Seattle–Rome route: the economics of a long-haul launch
item.description: Case study. The April 2026 launch added Alaska’s first European route. Demand, connections, seasonal schedules, and costs shape its business case.

item.title: Regulation B in 2026: the CFPB’s changes to fair-lending rules
item.description: Regulatory explainer. The April rule changes the treatment of disparate impact, discouragement, and special purpose credit programs. Here is the scope of the revision.

item.title: Warsh’s nomination hearing: how to assess Fed independence
item.description: Institutional explainer. Warsh’s April 2026 nomination hearing provides a starting point for examining the Fed’s mandate, accountability, and later decisions.

item.title: Tesla Q1 2026: the results behind the AI investment story
item.description: Earnings analysis. Revenue, automotive margins, and cash flow describe Tesla’s reported quarter. AI and autonomy plans require a separate assessment.

item.title: Sotomayor’s April 2026 apology: public remarks and judicial decisions
item.description: Court case study. An apology to a colleague can address personal comments while leaving the legal effect of a court order unchanged.

item.title: The Sam Altman-related attack case: reading the April 2026 charges
item.description: Legal case study. San Francisco’s charging announcement identifies the alleged incidents and offenses. Court decisions are needed to establish the outcome.

item.title: The April 2026 U.S.–Iran ceasefire report: scope and implementation
item.description: Diplomatic news archive. A temporary pause leaves questions about coverage, compliance, shipping, and attribution of later incidents.

item.title: Perma-Pipe’s board appointments: evaluating expertise and oversight
item.description: Case study. The April 2026 appointments raise practical questions about committee responsibilities, project risk, and capital allocation.

item.title: The Proudfoot rescue: what the Coast Guard’s April 2026 account shows
item.description: Case study. Four people were rescued near Moriches Inlet with no injuries reported. The official account separates the rescue from unanswered questions about the vessel.

item.title: The Temple Israel investigation: inspiration and direction are different claims
item.description: Public-safety case study. The FBI’s account of the March 2026 attack shows why evidence of motive must be separated from evidence of operational control.

item.title: Trump’s signature on paper currency: interpreting Treasury’s announcement
item.description: Currency explainer. The March 2026 announcement concerned a future design change. Production schedules and collector prices are separate questions.

item.title: Military deployment and diplomacy: reading the March 2026 report
item.description: Case study. Reuters’ account of expected troop movements illustrates why planning, arrival, and authorization for a mission must be tracked separately.

item.title: The March 2026 EPA climate challenge: what the petition concerns
item.description: Legal case study. A coalition of states and local governments challenged the repeal of the endangerment finding and vehicle standards.

item.title: Denver’s canceled César Chávez march: questions for public commemoration
item.description: Case study. The organizers’ March 2026 decision illustrates how communities respond to allegations about the people they commemorate.

item.title: Evaluating Fin-TTEC: questions for a fintech operations buyer
item.description: Product analysis. TTEC’s March 2026 launch offers a case study in assessing outsourced support, performance measures, and accountability.
